title: Mystery case, format 0.2 (merged: case.json plus every part it lists)
description: A case is a constraint puzzle over the story's fabula. Cards (entities, events, claims, rules, glosses) are what the player sees and connects. Slots are the open questions on cards (an event's agent, place, time...). Constraints rest on cards: once all of a constraint's premises are known it rules values out. The engine (engine/caseModel.js) builds slots from event and entity facets, claim truth slots and the declared slots; scripts/validate-case.js checks everything the schema cannot (references, quotes, uniqueness, theories, Holmes's steps, playability). Format 0.3 adds relations, propositions, rule schemas and verified inferences (docs/format-0.3.md).

facet_types.description: Facet name → what values it takes. A facet on an event or entity becomes the slot '<card id>.<facet>'.

windows.description: Ordered time points. A time slot takes one of these; 'before' compares their order.

day.description: Day number, 0 = the day of the crime; null = before the story.

reveal.description: A quote: where the story first reaches this time. Before it, the window is not offered as an answer.

scenes.description: The disclosure axis: the order in which the reader is told things.

questions.description: The case's headline questions; each points at a slot.

raised.description: A quote: where the story first raises the question.

thoughts_file.description: The case's annotated reading (thoughts.json): a careful reader's thoughts, checked by scripts/validate-thoughts.js. Holmes's steps come from it (engine/steps.js, Round 57): each thought that names an inference, and each that carries a conclusion of Holmes's (`concludes`).

mentions_file.description: The case's mentions file: which phrases in the text name each card (and each time window). Loaded separately; see engine/story.js.

mentions.description: Filled in from mentions_file by the loader.

state_places.description: Named place sets a location or possession track ranges over (plus 'elsewhere').

prompt.description: The question, with {0} for the thing.

state_conditions.description: Conditions a condition track may name (true/false in each window).

label.description: What the person is trying to do, as an answer: 'To lead the horse home'.

state_aims.description: Aims an intention track ranges over (what a person is trying to do), one vocabulary with the purposes of acts: an act's purpose is its agent's aim at its time.

state_splits.description: Splits of a window (or a part of one) at an event, into the part before and the part after it: <window>.before.<event> and <window>.after.<event>.

source.description: Verbatim quotes from the story. The validator finds each one (curly quotes, dashes, underscores and whitespace normalised).

flag.description: placeholder: a card standing for someone not yet identified (its identity is a slot). hypothetical: only mentioned as a possibility. fiction_within_story: a character's invention. implied: the text infers it rather than shows it. stereotype: period prejudice voiced in the story.

challenge_scene.description: The last scene before the solution is revealed: the fair-play cut.

teaser.description: What the player sees before reading: must give nothing away.

domainSpec.description: kinds: every entity card of these kinds (placeholders and fiction excluded). time: every window. values: a fixed list.

include_self.description: Add the slot's own card as a value: 'nobody else in the story'.

reveal.description: value → a quote: the value is offered as an answer only once the story has reached it.

facetValue.description: The true value; an array = the story narrows it to these values but never settles it; null = the story never says.

name.description: The case's own name for it (reports, authoring). The player never sees it: see names.

within.description: For places: the larger place this one is part of.

notes.description: Details the story adds after the first mention, each with the quote that reveals it.

from_description.description: Was the card's old description: still to be checked against the story so far.

traits.description: General properties a rule may range over (a variable with `trait`). Each shows on the card as a plain gloss, dated by the card's first mention or its quote, whichever is later.

names.description: What the player sees it called, in story order: the first must be given by a line read by the time the card appears.

summary.description: Topic cards only: what the topic covers, written for the game (a topic is a subject, not a thing in the story).

label.description: The case's own label (reports, authoring). The player never sees it: see labels.

fabula_order.description: True chronological order (the fabula axis); ties broken by this number inside one time window.

labels.description: What the player sees the event called, in story order: the first must be given by a line read by the time the card appears.

chain.description: Who passed it on before the one quoted (workstream 4, Round 89), first speaker first: each link's speaker, hearer and when.

files.description: An absence (via absence) the player files rather than is dealt (Round 83): the default rule that expected what did not happen, the windows it did not happen in, and the clue that would have registered it.

part_of.description: A part of a statement (workstream 4): dealt only when the player splits that statement, to trust or doubt apart (what was seen, what concluded).

said.description: What the clue tells for certain, whatever the player makes of its content (e.g. that the speaker was certain of it): true whenever the clue is held, doubted or not (workstream 4).

said_at.description: When the speaker said it, for his belief in it (default: the time of the scene that tells it).

asserts.description: What the claim says in slot terms. Becomes the constraint 'k.<claim id>' resting on the claim.

truth_slot.description: The claim may be false (testimony, opinion): whether it is true is a slot '<claim id>.truth'.

truth_undetermined.description: The story never settles whether this claim is true.

derived.description: A conclusion to be proved, not a clue to collect. Excluded from the uniqueness evidence.

stated_in.description: Where the story itself states the rule (often only in the explanation).

period.description: Knowledge an 1890s reader had and a modern one may not.

attaches_to.description: The cards this fact is about (and its topic card): it shows on them, and in 'ask' mode asking about any of them recalls it.

editorial.description: Written for the game; plays no part in the solution.

relevant_from.description: A quote: where the story first touches this fact's subject. With background facts shown 'when relevant', the fact appears there.

schema.description: The fact as a formula with variables, grounded when applied to cards.

formula.description: A ground formula the fact asserts outright (no variables).

strength.description: hard: always so; default: so unless a named defeater holds; heuristic: usually so.

id.description: Unique within the rule; the player raises it by this id against one application.

source.description: The story line that speaks of the exception; it cannot be raised before it is read.

formula.description: Over the rule's schema variables, grounded with each application's bind: what holds when the exception does. Checked against what the player holds: ruled out, open (a reservation) or established (a defeat).

unless.description: Exceptions (workstream 3): what would make the fact not apply. A plain string is text only; a named exception (id, text, source, formula) can be raised against one application of the rule.

rule.description: A background fact that serves as a premise. It is shown on the card(s) it attaches to, mixed with the period notes, so that it does not stand out as a clue.

reading.description: A slot that carries what old cards mean (docs/hypotheses.md, Q6): its value under each story re-reads the cards.

puzzle.description: An oddity a story of the night must explain (docs/hypotheses.md, Q3): the cards that show it, the annotated thought that reads it, and its explanations. No text of its own.

editorial.description: Written for the game, not taken from the story.

after.description: A quote from the story: the gloss shows only once the reader has reached it (when the card it explains is mentioned earlier than the thing it explains).

formula.description: A formula over slots (ground), or a schema with variables (rules). eq/ne/in/nin compare a term with values; same/diff compare two terms; before/not_after compare time slots (or {lit: window}); seq puts events in order within one window; forall/exists range a variable over cards; only sets a relation's last argument.

seq.description: Events in one window, in this order (claims only): the same window, and each pair's order question ord.<a>.<b> before.

only.description: [relation, fixedArg..., [cards for which it is true]]

label.description: The reasoning in words, as a player would read it.

by.description: Who in the story reasons this way ('editorial' = needed by the puzzle, not voiced by anyone).

truth.description: false: a character's wrong reasoning. The case reads it doubted (its truth comes out false); a player trusts it until they doubt it.

stated.description: Where a character states this inference in the story: the player is given it there.

rules.description: The rule applications the inference uses: each rule must be among its premises.

defeated_by.description: A false inference's application that the true story defeats (workstream 3): the id of the rule's named exception that holds. Verification keeps the application; the case's reading does not, and the validator checks the exception in the answer key.

pattern.description: deduction, elimination, abduction, coincidence, identification, prediction_confirmed…

asserted.description: Why this inference is not (yet) derivable by the engine from its premises.

implicit.description: A step the engine needs but a reader makes without noticing (no thought in thoughts.json names it): granted as soon as its premises are held, never gates, never scores, shown as following from its premises and doubtable (short chains Q4).

rests_on.description: The inferences the theory's holders drew, that it stands on.

holder_knows_by_scene.description: The holders know every claim the reader has by this scene, and every rule…

holder_lacks.description: …except these (typically the rules they never thought to apply).

false.description: Default true. A theory marked false: false is right, and must survive all the evidence.

order.description: The investigation axis: the order things were done.

thoughts.description: Thoughts (Holmes's steps, engine/steps.js) made before (requires) or by (yields) this action.
Thoughts (Holmes's steps, engine/steps.js) made before (requires) or by (yields) this action.

cue.description: Short, spoiler-free label for the read-on button.

dated.description: A name or label the player sees, with the line of the story that gives it: it shows only once that line has been read. 'editorial' marks a heading written for the game (topic cards).

term.description: A slot: its id, '?v.facet' (a slot of a bound card), or {rel: [name, arg...]} (a relation slot; an arg is a card id, '?v', or a slot whose value indexes the relation). Or {state: [name, thing, time]}: a declared state (location 'at', possession 'held', or a condition) of a card in a window; time is a window, '?w', or a time slot.

value.description: A literal value, or '?v' for a bound card.

varSpec.description: What a variable, quantifier or relation argument ranges over: entity kinds, events, or a list.

trait.description: Only cards that carry this trait (an entity's `traits`).

placeholder.description: range over the cards standing for someone not yet identified (flag placeholder), of the given kind(s)

condition.description: range over the declared state conditions

proposition.description: range over the propositions; in a state term the bound proposition names its knowledge track

statement.description: range over the statements (testimony, admission); in a state term the bound statement names its speaker's belief in it

relation.description: A relation between cards; every argument tuple is a slot rel.<id>.<arg>...

prompt.description: The question, with {0}, {1}… for the arguments.

answers.description: [arg..., value] rows; the rest take default_answer (null = left open).

open.description: Argument tuples the story leaves open.

outside.description: What the relation is for arguments outside its declared range when a slot's value falls there (default: an error).

proposition.description: An intermediate conclusion as a boolean slot p.<name>, and a card.

means.description: Its meaning in slot terms: the model adds a definition tying the two.

source.description: Lines that raise the question (workstream 3): the card is dealt at the first, as an event told directly is. Without it, a proposition comes with a clue or inference that speaks of it.

stateTrack.description: One thing in one aspect over the time windows the case declares: each window is a slot <id>.<window without 'w.'>; null = left open by the story.

believes.description: Belief (workstream 4): the proposition, or the statement (a claim: what the speaker said), believed or not; the track is st.<thing>.believes_<name>.

knows.description: Knowledge: the proposition the thing knows (or not); the track is st.<thing>.knows_<proposition>.

holders.description: Possession: the kinds of card that may hold it (default person, animal, group).
